newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen buoyed by Dow's record climb.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen buoyed by Dow's record climb.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are expected to recover on Wednesday, reversing their losses over the past two trading days as market participants gain encouragement from the Dow industrial's surge to an all-time high overnight, brokers said.
On Tuesday, the 225-share Nikkei average closed down 92.30 points or 0.46 percent at 20,157.02. September Nikkei futures slipped 100 points to close at 20,180.
"Trade has been volatile lately, but the Nikkei 225 will naturally rise on the Dow's surge," said Kenji Karikomi, deputy general manager at Daiwa Securities Co Ltd.

The Nikkei 225 index is ready to reflect the bullish sentiment in the United States, as "the index has been through enough of a technical adjustment," said a broker at a medium-sized Japanese securities house.
But brokers also said that any rise in the key stock index was likely to be capped by strong resistance at 20,500.

On Tuesday, the Dow soared 154.93 points to close at 8,061.65, eclipsing the previous record of 8,038.88, set on July 16, after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan delivered an upbeat report on the U.S. economy in his semi-annual report to Congress.
